source_refs.note: Topic 11.2.3 (Nomenclature of cycloalkanes) with Figure 11.3 and Quick Check 11.1, printed page 249.

blocks.text: Cycloalkanes are named by attaching the prefix ‘cyclo’ to the names of the alkanes possessing the same number of carbon atoms. Figure 11.3

blocks.alt: Four cyclohexane rings with side chains in condensed form. Ethylcyclohexane: CH2-CH3 on the ring. Isopropylcyclohexane: H3C-CH-CH3 with chain numbers 1 and 2; common name isopropylcyclohexane, IUPAC name 1-methylethylcyclohexane. 1,1,4-Trimethylcyclohexane: ring numbered 1 to 4, CH3 on carbon 4 and H3C and CH3 on carbon 1. n-Propylcyclohexane: CH2-CH2-CH3; IUPAC name propylcyclohexane.
blocks.caption: Figure 11.3: Naming cycloalkanes (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 11.3).
